summary: This paper gives a clean high-dimensional analysis of single-location regression showing that softmax attention attains Bayes risk in population while linear (and several natural alternatives) do not, then extends the comparison to a finite-sample ERM characterization via order parameters/replicas with matching numerics. The contribution is timely and well motivated by retrieval gaps, and the population-level results are convincing; the finite-sample/computational parts lean on non-rigorous replica arguments and an incomplete landscape/manifold analysis. Relative to recent ICLR theory accepts, this is a borderline-to-weak accept pending clearer scoping of computational claims and stronger finite-D statistical reporting.
strengths: Principled SLR formalization (spiked- and max-SLR, random lengths) that makes retrieval-style single-token dependence amenable to high-d analysis of true softmax, not only linearized attention.

Sharp population-level separation: softmax reaches Bayes risk under a natural condition on gν, while linear attention has explicit suboptimal asymptotics in ν and L, with useful comparisons isolating normalization vs. nonlinearity.

Order-parameter reduction yields actionable risk formulas; finite-α replica predictions align closely with large-scale local optimization, and the paper is generally honest about where softmax is no longer Bayes-optimal.

key_concerns.issue: Result 5.1—the main finite-sample characterization—is explicitly non-rigorous (replica symmetry), with rigor deferred to future replicon-style proofs for multi-index ERM; yet several computational/statistical conclusions rest on it.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: State replica claims as conjectures/predictions throughout the main text, add any available replicon checks or partial rigorous regimes, and separate rigorously proved population results from replica predictions in the abstract/contribution list.

key_concerns.issue: Approximation/optimization claims that one-pass SGD efficiently attains the population optimum rely on a manifold restriction, numerical stability checks, and acknowledged off-manifold local minima, without a complete landscape or GD convergence argument.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either prove local convergence on M under stated assumptions or substantially soften ‘efficiently attainable by one-pass SGD’ language and expand Appendix A.2 into a clear negative/positive landscape map with finite-D failure modes.

key_concerns.issue: Generality of the takeaway (‘statistical advantage of softmax’) is under-supported beyond a stylized two-direction attention class without queries/heads/depth, and alternatives are limited (linear, erf, softplus kernel) despite an intro framed around kernelized attention and SSMs.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Narrow claims to single-location attention predictors as analyzed, and add at least one broader comparison (e.g., another kernel ϕ, multi-query/multi-location variant, or explicit discussion of why SSM/gating is out of scope rather than implied by the empirical motivation).

key_concerns.issue: Finite-D validation (Fig. 3) reports agreement with theory for ND=10^4 and grid-searched regularization, but the main text does not make clear multi-seed variance, confidence intervals, or sensitivity to optimizer/init.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report means±std over seeds for test risk vs α, and ablate regularization and initialization (informed vs uninformed) in the main figure or a compact table.

key_concerns.issue: Positioning vs concurrent softmax-vs-linear and sequence multi-index works is present but brief; novelty relative to that line could be sharper for a main-track theory paper.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add an explicit contribution table contrasting model (variable L, gν, softmax nonlinearity), guarantees (Bayes vs ERM), and proof techniques against Cui/Troiani/Dragutinović/Barnfield concurrent threads.

questions_for_authors: Under what precise conditions (if any) do you expect the replica-symmetric prediction for Eσ(α) to fail, and have you checked the replicon eigenvalue along the fixed-point path in Fig. 3?
Does the softmax–linear gap persist with a learnable query (or CLS-query parameterization beyond the cited special case), multi-head mixing, or nonzero output noise at finite α?

For the hard phase of the Bayes-optimal curve (Fig. 3 black), can approximate message passing or another first-order method close the gap to EBO, or is softmax ERM information-theoretically suboptimal in a computationally hard regime?
How sensitive are Corollaries 4.3–4.4 and Fig. 2 to the choice of PL (e.g., heavy-tailed lengths) versus the reported Unif{1,2,3} / fixed-L cases?
calibration_check: Core claims about a population Bayes gap for softmax vs linear on SLR are well scoped and evidenced; broader retrieval/architecture conclusions and finite-sample optimality/computability claims are somewhat ahead of the rigorous and empirical support.

significance.justification: Explaining why softmax beats linearized/kernelized alternatives on retrieval-like dependence is highly relevant to ICLR, though impact is tempered by the stylized SLR abstraction.

novelty.justification: Extending sequence multi-index ideas to variable-length SLR with a genuine softmax analysis and sharp linear gaps is original enough, but sits close to concurrent multi-index/softmax-vs-linear work.

rigor.justification: Population Bayes/risk results and corollaries look sound; finite-sample ERM and SGD-efficiency arguments depend on replica symmetry and an incomplete manifold/landscape theory.

statistical_soundness.justification: Asymptotic characterizations are the right tool, and theory–simulation match is persuasive, but main-text finite-D results lack clear multi-seed error bars/significance reporting.

calibration_honesty.justification: Authors flag non-Bayes finite-α behavior, replica non-rigor, manifold caveats, missing queries, and activation-specific failure modes rather than overclaiming SOTA generality.

clarity.justification: Organization and contribution roadmap are clear; notation/order-parameter density will challenge non-stat-phys readers but remains standard for this literature.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard ICLR flow (intro, related work, model, population analysis, finite-sample analysis, experiments) with coherent sectioning and scoped contributions.

reproducibility.justification: Data model, activations, order-parameter equations, self-consistency updates, and regularization tuning are described in enough detail to reproduce if code/links were present.

related_work.justification: Retrieval tasks, kernelized attention, SSMs, and sequence multi-index methods are fairly covered, with concurrent work acknowledged, though delineation could be sharper.

figure_quality.justification: Captions for Figs. 2–3 and Table 1 cleanly support the Bayes gap and finite-α theory–ERM agreement; Fig. 1 is motivational reuse rather than new evidence.

breadth_generality.justification: Evidence spans two SLR variants and a few activations/α regimes, but not queries/heads/depth, SSM-style models, or broader retrieval formalisms implied by the motivation.

overall_recommendation.justification: Solid, useful theory with a clear softmax-vs-linear message and matching numerics, but replica/landscape gaps and limited generality keep it at a weak/borderline accept rather than a clear accept.
